current_row.boundary_rationale: A second self-address formula restarts the quest: דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי אֲנִ֤י עִם לִבִּי֙ (oshb:Eccl.1.16, byte tier) — the dibbarti verb itself, one of exactly two book-wide sites (sweep: 2 verses), is what marks this restart, not a wholesale shift away from the heart-idiom: the natan-plus-lev construction that opened the preceding row at 1:13, וְנָתַ֣תִּי אֶת לִבִּ֗י (oshb:Eccl.1.13, byte tier), recurs inside this very row at 1:17, וָאֶתְּנָ֤ה לִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת (oshb:Eccl.1.17, byte tier) — the same construction, disclosed here rather than implied absent. “I said to myself, “Behold, I have obtained for myself great wisdom…”” (web:Eccl.1.16) leads into the wisdom-versus-madness-and-folly inquiry of 1:17 and its verdict, “For in much wisdom is much grief; and he who increases knowledge increases sorrow.” (web:Eccl.1.18), which closes the row before the mirth experiment of the next chapter opens on a fresh amarti formula.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 1:16-18 as a continuation of the same unit as 1:12-15 was considered and rejected on the strength of the dibbarti verb itself (sweep: 2 verses) — a distinct first-person speech verb from the natan-plus-lev construction of 1:13, even though that same construction recurs within this row at 1:17.
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: Grief-verdict couplet (1:18) closes with no hevel token, unlike the quest units on either side of it -- a bare gnomic conclusion rather than a vanity-formula close.

items.class: E-06 register bleed carrying a byte-false cross-row claim (E-18 arm)
items.claim: The rival-defeating disclosure asserts that the natan-plus-lev construction 'opened the preceding row at 1:13'; 1:13 is that row's second verse, not its opening, and the assertion contradicts the neighbour row's own account of 1:13.
items.auditor_grounds: The preceding row's span Eccl.1.12-Eccl.1.15 opens at 1:12 with אֲנִ֣י קֹהֶ֗לֶת הָיִ֥יתִי מֶ֛לֶךְ (oshb:Eccl.1.12, byte tier); וְנָתַ֣תִּי אֶת לִבִּ֗י stands at 1:13 (oshb:Eccl.1.13, byte tier). The substantive recurrence the sentence exists to disclose is TRUE and survives the repair: וְנָתַ֣תִּי אֶת לִבִּ֗י (oshb:Eccl.1.13, byte tier) and וָאֶתְּנָ֤ה לִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת (oshb:Eccl.1.17, byte tier) are both natan-root plus lev, so the row's 'disclosed here rather than implied absent' posture is honest and only the positional attribution is defective. Not load-bearing - the restart driver is the dibbarti verb (sweep: 2 verses, 1:16 and 2:15), which the row cites with its digit.
items.proposed_change: boundary_rationale field repair: drop the positional row reference and the false 'opened' attribution, re-anchoring on the verse alone (e.g. 'the natan-plus-lev construction standing at 1:13 ... recurs inside this row at 1:17'). Span, refs, unit_type and confidence unaffected.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. The preceding row's span is Eccl.1.12-Eccl.1.15 and its opening verse begins אֲנִ֣י קֹהֶ֗לֶת הָיִ֥יתִי מֶ֛לֶךְ (oshb:Eccl.1.12, byte tier; the verse's first four tokens); the natan-plus-lev construction וְנָתַ֣תִּי אֶת לִבִּ֗י (oshb:Eccl.1.13, byte tier) stands in that row's SECOND verse, so the shipped clause 'the natan-plus-lev construction that opened the preceding row at 1:13' is false as a claim about the neighbour row, contradicts that row's own account (1:12 restates the royal self-identification; 1:13 'continues into the first wisdom inquiry'), and is a positional row reference the book's register purge bars outright. The recurrence the sentence exists to disclose is TRUE: וָאֶתְּנָ֤ה לִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת (oshb:Eccl.1.17, byte tier) is the same natan-root-plus-lev construction in a different inflected form (the 1:13 form recurs as a contiguous skeleton phrase at 2 verses book-wide, 1:13 and 8:16; the 1:17 form at 1 verse book-wide), so the 'disclosed here rather than implied absent' posture survives and the falsity is confined to the positional attribution. BOTH SIDES of the 1:15|1:16 seam weighed: 1:15 closes on the gnomic couplet וְחֶסְר֖וֹן לֹא יוּכַ֥ל לְהִמָּנֽוֹת (oshb:Eccl.1.15, byte tier) with no hevel refrain, and 1:16 opens on the self-address formula דִּבַּ֨רְתִּי אֲנִ֤י עִם לִבִּי֙ (oshb:Eccl.1.16, byte tier; sweep: 2 verses book-wide carry the dibbarti token, 1:16 and 2:15), the word-bound content-token intersection of 1:15 x 1:16 being empty; the formula onset decides the seam under the book's monologue rule, so the false clause is not load-bearing. Verdict: confirm at medium under the register lane's E-18 arm (a false cross-row claim, not load-bearing; low would understate a byte-false statement about a neighbour row's structure). Repair validated: re-anchoring on the verses alone ('the natan-plus-lev construction standing at 1:13 ... recurs inside this row at 1:17') is byte-sound provided 'recurs' is read as the same construction in different inflected forms rather than a word-bound identity; field repair only, no span effect.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The wine-and-works experiment opens with a distinct heart-formula, תַּ֣רְתִּי בְלִבִּ֔י (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier) — “I searched in my heart how to cheer my flesh with wine…” (web:Eccl.2.3) — sharing its root (tur) with 1:13's לִדְר֤וֹשׁ וְלָתוּר֙ (oshb:Eccl.1.13, byte tier), the finite tarti here differing from that verse's own infinitive form, not from its separate natan-root verb וְנָתַ֣תִּי. The row then runs an anaphoric accumulation across 2:4-2:8 (“I made myself great works. I built myself houses. I planted myself vineyards.”, web:Eccl.2.4, continuing through gardens, pools, servants, herds, and silver and gold) bound by the ethical dative li running unbroken across web:Eccl.2.4-Eccl.2.9 (sweep: 6 verses) and the mikol…lifnay…bi-Yerushalaim inclusio bracketing web:Eccl.2.7 and web:Eccl.2.9, and closes on the self-summary of 2:9-2:10, “So I was great, and increased more than all who were before me in Jerusalem.” (web:Eccl.2.9), before a fresh turning-formula opens the next row at 2:11.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the works catalogue from its wine-test introduction (2:3) was considered; it was rejected not on syntax — MT 2:4 opens asyndetically, הִגְדַּ֖לְתִּי מַעֲשָׂ֑י (oshb:Eccl.2.4, byte tier), a genuine clause break — but on the lexical cohesion the ethical dative li and the mikol…lifnay…bi-Yerushalaim inclusio supply across web:Eccl.2.4-Eccl.2.9.
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: Anaphoric first-person accumulation verbs (made/built/planted/bought/gathered) give this stretch a catalogue-like texture; it is kept as monologue_unit rather than list_catalogue because the enumeration is loosely-formed autobiographical narration, not the fixed et-plus-infinitive register template, which the book locates at 3:2-8 (3:1 being that catalogue's own introductory heading, not itself part of the infinitive series).

items.proposed_change: strongest_rejected_alternative / boundary_rationale field repair: replace the rejection ground with one that actually crosses 2:3|2:4 (e.g. the single first-person experiment frame opened at 2:3 whose self-benefit clauses 2:4-2:9 execute), or state plainly that the 2:3|2:4 clause break is conceded and the unit is held together on the experiment frame. items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. The rival field concedes the clause break, הִגְדַּ֖לְתִּי מַעֲשָׂ֑י (oshb:Eccl.2.4, byte tier; the verse's asyndetic first tokens), and rejects the split on two objects that both stop short of the contested 2:3|2:4 seam: the word-bound skeleton token li counts 0 at 2:3, then 2/1/1/2/2/1 across 2:4-2:9 and 0 at 2:10 (six verses, matching the row's digit, none of them 2:3), and the contiguous skeleton phrase lifnay-birushalaim returns 2 verses book-wide (2:7, 2:9). The word-bound content-token intersection of 2:3 x 2:4 is EMPTY, so nothing the row cites explains why 2:3 belongs with 2:4-2:10; the warrant offered never reaches the rival it is aimed at. BOTH SIDES of the seam weighed under the book's monologue rule (formula onsets open units): 2:3 closes on its purpose clause מִסְפַּ֖ר יְמֵ֥י חַיֵּיהֶֽם (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier) with no closural refrain, and 2:4 opens on a plain narrative perfect carrying no self-address or turning formula (the tarti frame תַּ֣רְתִּי בְלִבִּ֔י (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier) is unique, sweep: 1 verse book-wide; the turning formula u-faniti returns 2 verses, 2:11 and 2:12; no amarti, dibbarti, shavti or raiti token stands at 2:4), so no ruled onset device opens a unit at 2:4 and the rival fails on bytes the row never states. The outer seams are independently warranted (tarti at 2:3; the turning formula at 2:11), so the defect is a misdirected rival warrant, not load-bearing: confirm at medium. Repair validated with qualification: the experiment-frame ground is byte-sound (2:3's frame verb plus its purpose clause עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁר אֶרְאֶ֗ה אֵי זֶ֨ה ט֜וֹב לִבְנֵ֤י הָאָדָם֙ (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier), which the self-benefit catalogue of 2:4-2:9 executes) and may add the lexeme-level heart and wisdom bracket, וְלִבִּ֞י נֹהֵ֤ג בַּֽחָכְמָה֙ (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier) against כִּֽי לִבִּ֤י שָׂמֵ֨חַ֙ (oshb:Eccl.2.10, byte tier) and אַ֥ף חָכְמָתִ֖י עָ֥מְדָה לִּֽי (oshb:Eccl.2.9, byte tier), but only as root-level texture, never as word-bound identity (the 2:3 x 2:9 and 2:3 x 2:10 word-bound content intersections are also empty). current_row.boundary_rationale: A patterned companionship poem answers the solitary toiler of 4:8: טוֹבִ֥ים הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם מִן הָאֶחָ֑ד (oshb:Eccl.4.9, byte tier) — “Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor.” (web:Eccl.4.9) — develops across three parallel illustrations (falling, warmth, and resistance) before closing, “…and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.” (web:Eccl.4.12).
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping this stretch as monologue_unit (the parent's operative default) was considered and rejected: unlike the surrounding first-person narration, 4:9-12 carries no first-person verb at all and runs a three-clause conditional construction with three distinct lead particles -- כִּ֣י אִם (oshb:Eccl.4.10, byte tier), גַּ֛ם אִם (oshb:Eccl.4.11, byte tier), and וְאִֽם (oshb:Eccl.4.12, byte tier) -- not an identical repeated opener, a formal structure closer to the book's other patterned poems than to sustained autobiographical prose. saying_cluster was also considered and rejected: the four verses form one continuous, grammatically dependent illustration series -- each of 4:10-4:12 illustrates 4:9's own 'two are better than one' thesis, closing on a single capping image at 4:12 -- rather than detachable, independently-standing sayings, so wisdom_poem's patterned-poem category fits better than a cluster of sayings.
current_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
current_row.device_notes: Deviation disclosure: wisdom_poem is applied to a stretch inside the M parent, whose operative default is monologue_unit, because this unit's three-clause conditional construction-run and complete absence of a first-person verb match wisdom_poem's own operative category rather than the surrounding narration's form. This row's own opening verse continues a cross-seam ordinal device: the 'no second' construction, וְאֵ֥ין שֵׁנִ֖י (oshb:Eccl.4.10, byte tier), echoes web:Eccl.4.8's own וְאֵ֨ין שֵׁנִ֜י (oshb:Eccl.4.8, byte tier; this quoted span sits outside that verse's own ketiv/qere variant) -- the book's only 2-site occurrence of this ordinal clause (sweep: 2 verses) -- disclosed and weighed here: it does not override the independent shavti-restart boundary already established at web:Eccl.4.7-Eccl.4.8|Eccl.4.9, since a single echoed ordinal clause inside a four-verse illustration series does not by itself bind this unit to the verse before it.

items.class: seam warrant absent from the driver field / deferred to a boundary 'already established'
items.claim: The row states no affirmative byte warrant for either of its own seams: the opening seam is deferred to a boundary 'already established' by the preceding unit's shavti restart at 4:7, which warrants that unit's opening rather than the 4:8|4:9 seam, while two byte warrants standing at the seam itself go uncited.
items.auditor_grounds: boundary_rationale offers only continuity ('answers the solitary toiler of 4:8'), the unit's shape and its closing quotation; the only boundary-relevant byte evidence in the row - no first-person verb, the three-particle conditional run - sits in strongest_rejected_alternative as a unit_type argument, and device_notes then defers the seam to 'the independent shavti-restart boundary already established at web:Eccl.4.7-Eccl.4.8|Eccl.4.9'. The shavti restart stands in 4:7, i.e. it establishes the PRECEDING unit's opening (sweep shavti/veshavti: 3 verses - 4:1, 4:7, 9:11), and the preceding row as embedded likewise argues its own opening and 4:8's content but never its close. Two byte warrants at the seam are available and uncited: 4:8 closes on the verdict גַּם זֶ֥ה הֶ֛בֶל וְעִנְיַ֥ן רָ֖ע הֽוּא (oshb:Eccl.4.8, byte tier), a closural refrain, and 4:9 opens on the comparative טוֹבִ֥ים הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם מִן הָאֶחָ֑ד (oshb:Eccl.4.9, byte tier) - a genuine tov-min construction with an intervening token, which is why it escapes the contiguous tov-min adjacency sweep and must be checked as a construction. Not alone load-bearing: the span itself is not challenged and the form evidence in the rival field is byte-true.
items.proposed_change: boundary_rationale field repair: state the row's own seam warrant from the seam's own bytes (4:8's closural hevel verdict and 4:9's tov-min comparative opener) and move the form evidence out of the unit_type rival into the boundary case. No respan proposed.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes both ways. The shavti turn stands at 4:7, וְשַׁ֧בְתִּי אֲנִ֛י וָאֶרְאֶ֥ה (oshb:Eccl.4.7, byte tier; sweep: 3 verses book-wide carry the shavti/veshavti token, 4:1, 4:7, 9:11), which establishes the PRECEDING unit's opening at 4:6|4:7, not the 4:8|4:9 seam this row's device_notes assigns to it ('the independent shavti-restart boundary already established at web:Eccl.4.7-Eccl.4.8|Eccl.4.9'); the embedded 4:7-4:8 row likewise argues its opening and 4:8's content but never its close, so the seam is un-argued from both rows. boundary_rationale names no seam device at all (continuity 'answers the solitary toiler of 4:8', the opening quotation, an illustration count and the closing quotation), and the only form evidence (no first-person verb; three distinct lead particles) sits in the unit_type rival. BOTH SIDES of 4:8|4:9 weighed from bytes: 4:8 closes on the verdict refrain גַּם זֶ֥ה הֶ֛בֶל וְעִנְיַ֥ן רָ֖ע הֽוּא (oshb:Eccl.4.8, byte tier; the contiguous skeleton phrase gam-zeh-hevel returns 13 verses book-wide and the appended ve-inyan-ra 1 verse), a refrain close under the book's rule; 4:9 opens on the comparative טוֹבִ֥ים הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם מִן הָאֶחָ֑ד (oshb:Eccl.4.9, byte tier), a genuine tov-min construction whose plural first token and intervening subject keep it out of both the contiguous tov-min adjacency inventory and the tov-opener inventory (sweep: 3 verses book-wide carry the plural tovim, 4:9, 7:10, 11:6, only 4:9 verse-initial; the phrase min-ha-echad 1 verse); the word-bound content-token intersection of 4:8 x 4:9 is empty. Both sides decide the seam independently of the shavti restart, and the row's form claims re-derive true (no first-person -ti form and no ani token in 4:9-4:12; lead particles ki-im, gam-im, ve-im at their own refs). The rear seam also holds: 4:12 closes לֹ֥א בִמְהֵרָ֖ה יִנָּתֵֽק (oshb:Eccl.4.12, byte tier) and 4:13 opens on the inventory tov-opener ט֛וֹב יֶ֥לֶד מִסְכֵּ֖ן וְחָכָ֑ם (oshb:Eccl.4.13, byte tier), intersection empty. The span is unchallenged and the seam byte-sound, so the defect is an absent/misdirected warrant in the driver field: confirm at medium. Repair validated with qualification: restating the seam from 4:8's refrain close and 4:9's comparative onset is byte-sound, but 4:9 must be cited as a construction check with the digits above, not as an inventory site, and the cross-seam ordinal echo ve-ein-sheni (sweep: 2 verses, 4:8 and 4:10) stays disclosed as the row already does. Field repair only; no respan.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The mourning word “אֵ֗בֶל” (oshb:Eccl.7.2, byte tier), in the bare construct “בֵּֽית אֵ֗בֶל”, “house of mourning” (web:Eccl.7.2), opens the cluster at “בֵּֽית אֵ֗בֶל מִלֶּ֨כֶת֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית מִשְׁתֶּ֔ה” (oshb:Eccl.7.2, byte tier), “It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting” (web:Eccl.7.2). The same word stands again at the cluster's close, but with a prefixed preposition rather than a bare repetition: “בְּבֵ֣ית אֵ֔בֶל” (oshb:Eccl.7.4, byte tier from its own verse), in “לֵ֤ב חֲכָמִים֙ בְּבֵ֣ית אֵ֔בֶל וְלֵ֥ב כְּסִילִ֖ים בְּבֵ֥ית שִׂמְחָֽה” (oshb:Eccl.7.4, byte tier), “The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth” (web:Eccl.7.4). The bracket phrase as quoted at the opening collates byte tier against its own verse but only skeleton tier against oshb:Eccl.7.4, whose attested form carries the prefixed “in” that the opening's bare construct lacks. The driver that actually carries the boundary is the mourning word itself: “אֵ֗בֶל” / “אֵ֔בֶל” is word-bound identical at skeleton tier across the two ends and collates accent-stripped as a pointed form, and it is book-exclusive to this span (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, both inside the span, none elsewhere), matching neither excluded neighbour at any tier. Internal chaining is thin but real: the span's two adjacent pairs share one token apiece -- “ט֞וֹב” (oshb:Eccl.7.2) / “ט֥וֹב” (oshb:Eccl.7.3) (“good/better”) across web:Eccl.7.2-Eccl.7.3, and “לֵֽב” (oshb:Eccl.7.3) / “לֵ֤ב” (oshb:Eccl.7.4) (“heart”) across web:Eccl.7.3-Eccl.7.4 -- the honest thin-cohesion hold this cluster's confidence reflects. The middle verse, web:Eccl.7.3 (“Sorrow is better than laughter”), carries its own causal “for” clause on the same mourning-versus-mirth axis and sits inside the bracket rather than opening a new unit. The cluster is held apart from web:Eccl.7.1 (the mourning word matches it at no tier) and, less cleanly, from web:Eccl.7.5-Eccl.7.7: the fools word, “כְּסִילִ֖ים” (oshb:Eccl.7.4), recurs word-bound into web:Eccl.7.5 and also into web:Eccl.7.9 (sweep: 3 verses book-wide, web:Eccl.7.4, web:Eccl.7.5, web:Eccl.7.9), and a wise-root family bridges web:Eccl.7.4 into web:Eccl.7.5 and web:Eccl.7.7 across two attested spellings -- the plural “חֲכָמִים֙” (oshb:Eccl.7.4, sweep: 3 verses book-wide) and the singular “חָכָ֑ם” (oshb:Eccl.7.5) / “חָכָ֑ם” (oshb:Eccl.7.7) (sweep: 7 verses book-wide, 2 of them in this chapter). Both echoes are topic-level -- a shift from the mourning/mirth axis to the rebuke/song-of-fools axis at 7.5, then to an unrelated corruption saying at 7.7 -- rather than a repeated cohesion phrase, so neither pulls those verses into the bracket. A further rival stands over web:Eccl.7.3-Eccl.7.6 on the laughter root, “מִשְּׂחֹ֑ק” (oshb:Eccl.7.3) / “שְׂחֹ֣ק” (oshb:Eccl.7.6) (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, web:Eccl.7.3 and web:Eccl.7.6), straddling this cluster's closing seam; but that envelope's own adjacent chain breaks at web:Eccl.7.5-Eccl.7.6, which share no word-bound content token, while this span's own chain holds at both adjacent pairs -- the mourning word, not the laughter root, is this span's driver.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating web:Eccl.7.1-Eccl.7.8 as one continuous cluster on the chapter's tov-opener anaphora was considered, since the anaphora is real (7 of 12 book-wide tov-openers stand in this chapter), but web:Eccl.7.1 shares no phrase with this bracket and web:Eccl.7.7 breaks the pattern outright, so a single mechanical span would erase real seams rather than argue past them. A closer rival, the laughter-root envelope over web:Eccl.7.3-Eccl.7.6, was also considered and rejected: its own adjacent chain breaks at the token-empty web:Eccl.7.5-Eccl.7.6 seam, while this span's mourning-word bracket holds at both adjacent pairs and is book-exclusive to its own bounds.

current_row.boundary_rationale:
This admonition spans the whole zone as one imperative/jussive-framed unit. The zone's directive forms cluster at its two ends: שַׁלַּ֥ח (oshb:Eccl.11.1, tier: byte), "send", opens the counsel, matching “Cast your bread on the waters” (web:Eccl.11.1); תֶּן (oshb:Eccl.11.2, tier: byte), "give", continues it, matching “Give a portion to seven, yes, even to eight” (web:Eccl.11.2); and the unit closes with זְרַ֣ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte), "sow", paired with the negative אַל תַּנַּ֣ח (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte), "do not let...rest", matching “In the morning sow your seed...in the evening don't withhold your hand” (web:Eccl.11.6). The three middle verses carry no second-person directive at all: v.3 opens a conditional protasis, אִם...עַל הָאָ֣רֶץ (oshb:Eccl.11.3, tier: byte); v.4 is a participial clause with a negated prefix-conjugation, שֹׁמֵ֥ר ר֖וּחַ לֹ֣א יִזְרָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.11.4, tier: byte); and v.5 is a comparative declarative. This directive distribution, imperatives at the frame's two ends bracketing a directive-free middle, is what fixes the unit's own bounds rather than any split within it.

Three byte-grounded binders carry across the zone's internal seams. The negated-knowledge refrain interlocks the opening, middle and close: לֹ֣א תֵדַ֔ע (oshb:Eccl.11.2, tier: byte) collates at accent-stripped tier against כָּ֗כָה לֹ֤א תֵדַע֙ (oshb:Eccl.11.5, tier: byte), and אֵֽינְךָ֤ יוֹדֵ֨עַ֙ (oshb:Eccl.11.5, tier: byte) collates at skeleton tier against אֵֽינְךָ֨ יוֹדֵ֜ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte); each attested form is book-exclusive to this span (sweep: 2 verses book-wide for the know-negation, web:Eccl.11.2 and web:Eccl.11.5; sweep: 2 verses book-wide for the negated-existential form, web:Eccl.11.5 and web:Eccl.11.6), with all four sites falling inside this unit. The seam at 11:2/11:3 itself carries a repeated phrase, עַל הָאָֽרֶץ (oshb:Eccl.11.2, tier: byte) against עַל הָאָ֣רֶץ (oshb:Eccl.11.3, tier: byte), word-bound at skeleton tier (sweep: 7 verses book-wide, and 11:2/11:3 the only adjacent pair among them). A third binder ties the declarative middle to the closing imperative: the same triliteral sowing root (ז-ר-ע) stands in יִזְרָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.11.4, tier: byte) and in זְרַ֣ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte), different inflected forms of the one root, not a word-bound identity, but book-exclusive to this span (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, both inside it). No byte warrant separates any internal seam that these three binders do not themselves cross.

Both outer bounds hold clean on content rather than chapter numbering: the back seam shares with the preceding verse only a causal particle, a function word, and that verse closes its own sentence zone (web:Eccl.10.20); the forward seam shares with the following verse only the object marker, and that verse opens the light-frame that begins the aging-allegory zone (web:Eccl.11.7).
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading web:Eccl.11.1-Eccl.11.2 as its own admonition_unit, separate from the verses that follow, is rejected from the bytes: its two members share no content token with each other, while the negated-knowledge refrain and the repeated on-the-earth phrase both carry directly across the 11:2/11:3 seam that split would have to hold.
